title: Optimal-query fully dynamic text indexing
formal: Is there a deterministic fully dynamic index for a fixed-alphabet string with linear-word space, polylogarithmic amortized character edits and O(m+occ) worst-case pattern-reporting queries?
definitions:
Fix a finite alphabet of at least two symbols and a maximum permitted text length N≥2. The current string T initially is empty and has length n≤N. Insert(c,i), for 0≤i≤n, inserts c before position i; Delete(i), for 0≤i<n, removes that character and shifts later positions. All edits are permanent until changed by later arbitrary edits. Query(P) receives a nonempty pattern of length m explicitly as one symbol per word and must output every integer i with 0≤i≤n−m and T[i,…,i+m−1]=P, once each in any order; occ is the number of outputs. Overlapping occurrences count. Queries do not change the text.

Use a uniform word-RAM with Θ(log(N+2)) bits per word, standard arithmetic and Boolean operations, and no advice. Maintain O(n+1) words at every stage, in addition to the read-only pattern and write-only output during queries; temporary query workspace is O(n+m+1). Initialization costs O(1). For any sequence, total time is O(U log^c(N+2)+∑queries(m+occ)+1) for an absolute c, with each individual query taking O(m+occ) worst-case time. Removed text storage must be reclaimed. N controls word length and edit bound; current n controls stored space.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of all stated guarantees, or prove the precise target impossible. State any complexity hypothesis used in a conditional impossibility. Append-only construction, ephemeral edits or additive log N query overhead do not meet this specification.
context: The recent paper handles edits immediately undone before the next independent edit. That model is weaker than accumulating arbitrary edits to the indexed text.
why: This seeks an optimal reporting interface that survives arbitrary edits throughout a text.

import_provenance.original_statement: Can a length-n text over a fixed alphabet be maintained in O(n) machine words with polylogarithmic amortized time per single-character insertion or deletion and O(m+occ) worst-case time to report all occurrences of a queried length-m pattern? Edits may occur at arbitrary positions, and the word size is Θ(log n).
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial strengthening of Ferragina and Grossi’s dynamic-indexing problem. Ephemeral edits that are immediately undone and append-only texts are weaker models.

sentences: Characters can be inserted or removed at arbitrary current positions.
A query reports every occurrence of a new pattern in the current text.
Output positions refer to the text after all prior edits.
Space is linear in current text length, while word size uses a supplied maximum.
The desired query time has no extra logarithmic term.
